clue.text: Clerks, chipper unless provoked

indicators.note: something provoked is stirred up and agitated, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: Office workers stay cheerful as long as nobody winds them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chipper' looks like a description of the clerks' mood, but it and 'unless' are simply the raw letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pencil-pushers is a mildly scornful informal term for office workers doing routine paperwork, which is what clerks are.

clue.text: Poet Laureate (republican) embraces queen: means to sort out future

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug and wrap one's arms around, so the outer letters enclose another piece

parts.note: PL are the initials of Poet Laureate
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
Queen Anne, the British monarch of the early 1700s

explanation.surface: A republican-minded poet laureate hugging the queen sounds like a scene about the monarchy's future.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'republican' looks like a political aside about the poet, but it supplies a letter to join the initials before they wrap around the queen's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A planner is a diary or organiser used to arrange appointments and tasks ahead of time, a tool for ordering what lies ahead.

clue.text: Run around collecting gold somewhere near Hawaii

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in and hold it, so one piece goes inside the other
turned around means moved about into a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the word taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone dashes about gathering gold on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters of 'Run' are rearranged to N-RU and gold's symbol slips in after the N. Nauru is a tiny Pacific island nation, though 'near Hawaii' is generous: it lies thousands of miles away.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a small island republic in the central Pacific, so it is one of the places in the same broad ocean region as the American islands.

clue.text: Everyman's 'friends' seen to include a group of antelopes

parts.note: the setter Everyman speaking of himself: 'Everyman is' becomes I'M

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: pals are friends
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter's so-called friends turn out to be a herd of antelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often refers to himself by his pseudonym, so 'Everyman's' means 'I am', shortened. The single letter A sits inside the friends, between the L and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Impalas are slender African antelopes, and the plural names several of those animals together, which matches a herd.

clue.text: Mix a Puerto Rican cocktail for nearby star

indicators.note: a cocktail is a blend of shaken ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: all four words supply the fodder, including the verb that looks like the instruction

explanation.surface: A bartender's instruction for making a Caribbean drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' looks like the signal to rearrange, but it is part of the fodder, providing the X; the true signal is 'cocktail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proxima Centauri is the closest known star to the Sun, a little over four light years away, so it is our nearest stellar neighbour.

clue.text: Take out fancy coffees, skipping college

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement
skipping something means missing it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: the word taken as written
C is a common abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: Getting elaborate coffees to take away instead of going to college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' suggests a takeaway order, but it means to defeat or get rid of. Remove the C from the coffees before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: To see off an opponent is to defeat or dispose of them, as to take out a rival means to eliminate them.

clue.text: Ray, trembling with desire, producing rebel movie

indicators.note: trembling means shaking, and shaken letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the name taken as written
the word taken as written; 'with' joins it to the name

explanation.surface: A man called Ray quivers with longing and makes a rebellious film.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray and desire together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy Rider is the 1969 counterculture road film starring Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper, a classic of youthful rebellion.

clue.text: Primarily, somewhere African, occupying the ocean, manifestly equatorial!

definitions.text: somewhere African, occupying the ocean, manifestly equatorial

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.words: somewhere African, occupying the ocean, manifestly equatorial
parts.note: the initials of the seven words

explanation.surface: A description of an African island country sitting in the sea on the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the instruction and the description: the initial letters spell the island, and the words describe it. Sao Tome is an island in the Gulf of Guinea lying almost exactly on the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: Sao Tome, part of Sao Tome and Principe, is an African island state in the Atlantic straddling the equatorial line.

clue.text: Pasta accompaniment: some asparagus

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so just part of the following word is used

parts.note: the letters sit inside the vegetable's name

explanation.surface: A vegetable side served alongside pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters sits in the middle of the vegetable's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragu is an Italian meat-based sauce traditionally served over pasta such as tagliatelle.

clue.text: Conversion of temperature scale in employment file

indicators.note: converting a temperature scale means switching from Fahrenheit to Celsius, so one scale's letter is swapped for the other's

parts.note: a profession is a line of employment

explanation.surface: Converting a temperature scale on a document in a job file.
explanation.walkthrough: F for Fahrenheit becomes C for Celsius within the job word. 'File' looks like a document but is a line of people walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a line of people one behind another, and a procession is people moving forward in such a line.

clue.text: When startled, pets rejected unpleasant modified lettuce, perhaps

indicators.note: modified means changed in form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
something rejected is sent back, so these letters run backwards
startled can be read as having its start removed, so letters are taken away

parts.note: the word read backwards
the word taken as written

explanation.surface: Frightened pets turn their noses up at some nasty, altered lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of pets reversed from 'unpleasant', leaving six letters to rearrange. 'Lettuce' looks like part of the pets' meal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is an annual: a plant that completes its life cycle within one growing season, so it is an example.

clue.text: Fashionable class, Old Norse, to sell out

parts.note: in means fashionable
a form is a school class in Britain
ON is the standard abbreviation for Old Norse

explanation.surface: A trendy group studying an ancient Scandinavian language decides to betray its principles.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group, as in 'the sixth form'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone out is to betray them, and informing on someone is betraying them to the authorities.

clue.text: Perhaps electrician winds item — a bobbin, ultimately

parts.note: the trades are the trade winds

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: An electrician coils wire around something, ending with a bobbin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like a verb about coiling wire, but it is the noun: the trades are the steady tropical trade winds.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrician is a skilled manual worker in a trade, so the general term covers him as one example among plumbers and joiners.

clue.text: Lying down, topless — welcome

indicators.note: topless means without a top, and in a vertical entry the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for down
a reception is a welcome

explanation.surface: Someone lying down, without a top on, greets a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying down' reads as one phrase about resting, but 'Lying' alone is the definition and 'down' gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying, used as a noun, is the act of telling falsehoods, which is deception or deliberate misleading of others.

clue.text: Vain movie star? Sounds like it

indicators.note: sounds like means the spoken word matches another when heard

parts.note: a film star is a screen idol

explanation.surface: Asking whether a vain film star is what it describes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' looks like a jibe at the star's ego, but it means futile, as in 'idle threats'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in the sense of useless or futile matches idle, as in idle threats or idle hopes that come to nothing.

clue.text: Important part of your foot

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the curved section of the sole between heel and ball

explanation.walkthrough: 'Important' looks like it describes the foot part, but it is a separate meaning: chief or principal, as in arch-enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective the word means chief or principal, and as a noun it is the raised curve under the sole.

clue.text: A nationalist idiot in Belgian city

parts.note: taken as written
N is an abbreviation for nationalist
a twerp is a silly or foolish person

explanation.surface: A foolish flag-waver turns up in a Belgian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twerp' is informal British for a foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major port and the largest city of Flanders in northern Belgium.

clue.text: Partially downgrades car tested by mathematician

indicators.note: partially means only in part, so a stretch of the following letters is used

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A mathematician's test results in a car being downgraded.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is spread across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third.
explanation.definitionFit: Rene Descartes, the French philosopher, invented Cartesian coordinates and is a founder of analytic geometry.

clue.text: In Perth, girl almost admitted to cricket club? Excellent

indicators.note: being admitted to somewhere means being let inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: CC is the abbreviation for cricket club

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Perth is in Scotland, where a girl is a lassie

explanation.surface: A young woman in Perth nearly gets into the local cricket club, and someone approves.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Scottish city, not the Australian one; the location tells you to use the Scottish word for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic describes something of the highest quality, a first-rate example of its kind, matching an outstanding thing.

clue.text: Carries out clobber

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the verb, brings about or accomplishes
second meaning: British slang for one's belongings or gear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb meaning to hit, but it is British slang for clothing and possessions, as in personal effects.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect a change is to bring it about, and personal effects are belongings, the same thing as clobber or gear.

clue.text: Suffering cold, student leaves, being disdainful

indicators.note: to leave is to depart, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: someone with a cold has the sniffles
L for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A student with a cold goes home, looking down on everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on British cars, and so stands for a student. 'Leaves' looks like a noun or a departure, but it tells you to drop that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sniffy is behaving in a scornful, superior way, looking down one's nose, which is a disdainful attitude.

clue.text: Can love and hugs return? Quickly!

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to pet someone is to caress or cuddle them

explanation.surface: A pleading question about whether affection can come back, followed by impatience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb opening a question, but it is the noun for a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom telling a driver to press the accelerator, an urgent command to go faster or hurry up.

clue.text: Notice fissure at sea

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
a rift is a crack or split

explanation.surface: Spotting a crack while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a short advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: At sea can mean confused or lost, and literally a boat floating with no mooring, both senses shared by adrift.

clue.text: Frailnesses regularly hidden; hairdresser might suggest one

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Weaknesses are concealed, and a stylist offers a treatment to cover them.
explanation.walkthrough: A rinse is a temporary hair colour, often suggested to disguise grey, so the surface about hiding frailties fits neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a temporary tint applied to the hair, a treatment that a stylist might recommend to a client.

clue.text: Not quite slim and small, having eaten more than three biscuits

indicators.note: what has been eaten is inside, so one piece goes within another
not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: petite means slight and slender
the next number up
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A slender, little person nearly stays thin despite eating several biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slim and small' looks like one description, but the two words give separate pieces; the S then swallows the number that comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Petits fours are small fancy cakes or biscuits served with coffee after a meal, so the plural matches biscuits.

clue.text: Agreeable resort

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the French Riviera city

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a pleasant holiday spot; split, one word is an adjective and the other names a seaside city in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pleasant, and the city on the Cote d'Azur is a famous Mediterranean holiday destination.

clue.text: Who'd make pale ale? Meanies

parts.note: surface reading: brewers producing a light beer
setter's reading: people who grab a P, the abbreviation for a coin, and put it in front of the beer word

explanation.surface: Wondering which tightwads would brew a light beer.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for a British penny; pinching one and sticking it on 'ale' turns it into 'pale', so whoever does that is literally pinching a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanies are stingy people reluctant to spend money, and those who count every coin are called this informally.
